note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of treatment options following recent biopsy confirmation of ISUP grade group 2 prostate cancer with high-risk architectural features.

Long-standing referral for management of prostate cancer. The patient is a 68-year-old secondary school teacher who recently relocated to live with his sister, though his spouse remains the primary next-of-kin contact. He has a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia and hypercholesterolaemia, currently managed with tamsulosin and a combination of atorvastatin and simvastatin. He is a non-smoker, consumes minimal alcohol, and maintains an active lifestyle with regular cycling. A surveillance colonoscopy was recently completed by gastroenterology without significant findings. His IPSS score is 3/35, indicating only mild lower urinary tract symptoms. He reports no new constitutional symptoms or bone pain.

On digital rectal examination, the prostate is smooth and non-nodular, consistent with a clinical T stage of cT1c. General examination is unremarkable, with no signs of lymphadenopathy or bony tenderness. Vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 138/77 mmHg and a heart rate of 71 bpm.
